Thought: To determine the correct ordering of d orbitals according to their energy in the metal complex Pt(NH3)3Cl2, I need to consider the crystal field splitting in a square planar complex, as platinum typically forms square planar complexes with ligands like NH3 and Cl. In square planar complexes, the splitting of the d orbitals typically follows the order: \(\mathrm{d}_{x^2-y^2}\) (highest energy) > \(\mathrm{d}_{xy}\) > \(\mathrm{d}_{z^2}\) > \(\mathrm{d}_{xz} = \mathrm{d}_{yz}\) (lowest energy). 

This is because the \(\mathrm{d}_{x^2-y^2}\) orbital has the highest energy due to direct overlap with the ligands on the x and y axes. The \(\mathrm{d}_{xy}\) orbital is next as it lies in the plane of the ligands. The \(\mathrm{d}_{z^2}\) orbital is less affected by the ligand field because it extends along the z-axis. The \(\mathrm{d}_{xz}\) and \(\mathrm{d}_{yz}\) orbitals have the lowest energy because they are oriented between the axes and experience less direct overlap with the ligands.

By comparing this reasoning to the given options, option C matches the expected order for a square planar complex.
